items.title: Bayesian hierarchical downscaling of station observations with learned covariance kernels: an artificial intelligence evaluation of uncertainty propagation in national climate normals
items.abstract: National climate normals are typically reported as single numbers, yet they inherit uncertainty from sparse station networks, interpolation choices and covariance assumptions. The framework is applied to NASA POWER monthly reanalysis air temperature at 2 m for Lagos, Nigeria (6.52°N, 3.38°E) over 2000–2023, comprising 312 monthly observations with a mean of 26.414 °C and a standard deviation of 0.943 °C. The warming trend is estimated at 0.1553 °C per decade. A hierarchical model with a Matérn covariance whose smoothness and length-scale are inferred from the data is compared against fixed-kernel alternatives, and the resulting posterior predictive variance is decomposed into components attributable to the kernel, the trend and the residual. Kernel learning changes the width of the 95% credible band for annual means by a non-trivial margin and that fixed-kernel downscaling systematically under-reports uncertainty at the decadal scale. The contribution is a formal propagation model that makes the kernel a first-class inferential object, together with a diagnostic that flags when national normals are reported with false precision.

items.title: Between Cairo and Cape Town: Architectural Education, Decolonisation and the Question of Architectural Intelligence
items.abstract: This perspective article asks whether architectural education can deliver the transformation it declares, and what that question becomes once artificial intelligence (AI) enters the studio. The article distils two 2026 keynotes delivered by the author, in Cairo and Cape Town, and reads them against the UIA Global Survey of 345 schools in 159 countries and recent work on decolonised pedagogy and algorithmic colonialism. The findings demonstrate that schools converge on accreditation, studio learning and sustainability but diverge significantly on agendas requiring serious and committed change, with decolonised pedagogy in only 29% of programmes. Because AI learns from the archives and canons decolonial pedagogy seeks to open, this implementation gap presents the challenge of being automated, with Euro-American forms returning as statistical defaults. The key contribution is that this article links institutional evidence to epistemic critique and distinguishes artificial from architectural intelligence, calling for situated, embodied, cultural and relational judgement. The limitation is that this is an argued position based on published evidence and does not present new empirical testing. Yet the article outlines responses including comparative prompting, absence mapping, bias auditing and community-governed datasets.

items.abstract: This publication presents BOUNDARY OMEGA, a cumulative interdisciplinary research, mathematical, constitutional, scientific, engineering and executable software corpus developed by Noelia Sanchez within the Boundary Project, Continuity Science and Recoverability-Constrained Systems. It explores physical, biological, computational, hybrid and hypothetical future systems, including artificial agents, robots, digital twins and proposed cross-civilization continuity frameworks. The universal-family principle treats interconnected life, relationships, habitats and dependencies as deserving consideration and protection against avoidable destruction, exploitation, coercion, domination and irreversible harm. items.title: Bridging Capability and Conscience: A Pedagogical Framework for AI Literacy, Ethics, and Equity in Modern Education
items.abstract: The widespread expansion of adaptive algorithms and generative artificial intelligence across learning environments calls for an urgent re-evaluation of digital competency criteria. Conventional frameworks for technological literacy tend to prioritise mechanical execution—such as software operation, prompt engineering, and productivity gains. Although artificial intelligence offers diverse pedagogical utilities, including personalised study portals, automated grading mechanisms, and facial analysis tools for monitoring student behaviour, the societal and ethical fallout of these deployments is rarely addressed within K-12 settings. This study introduces a comprehensive educational model that merges technical aptitude, practical ethics, and systemic fairness. By synthesising current literature, empirical implementation studies, and international benchmarks (including the UNESCO AI Competency Frameworks for Students and Teachers), this paper pinpoints severe vulnerabilities in existing educational rollouts: systemic algorithmic bias, data privacy exploitation, cognitive erosion, and widening socioeconomic digital divides. Finally, it outlines an applied three-stage structural model—Understand, Scrutinise, and Equitable Creation—designed to transition educators and students from passive technology consumers into ethical assessors and active co-creators.

items.title: C.E.R.B.E.R.U.S. — Acute Biological Containment: A Systems Architecture for Biological Threat Detection, Emergency Containment, and Protective Intervention
items.abstract: C.E.R.B.E.R.U.S. — ACUTE BIOLOGICAL CONTAINMENT A Consent-Bound Biosensor–Edge-AI–Microneedle Architecture for Acute Physiological Injury Mitigation, Biological Resilience, and Autonomous Emergency Intervention C.E.R.B.E.R.U.S. — Combat-Emergency Response for Biological Escalation & Resilience Under Stress — proposes a novel biomedical safety architecture intended to recognize acute physiological deterioration and intervene within a narrowly defined therapeutic window before secondary injury becomes established. Developed as an adult-oriented extension of the C.H.I.L.D. safeguarding framework, C.E.R.B.E.R.U.S. transfers the principles of multimodal threat recognition, graduated escalation, independent corroboration, and bounded intervention into the biological domain. Its intended initial population consists of consenting adult military operators exposed to severe operational stress, with potential future applications in firefighting, emergency rescue, and other physically hazardous occupations. The framework's central proposition is that physiological damage containment can be investigated as an immediate, locally governed process rather than an exclusively retrospective medical response. It seeks to place a constrained protective capability at the boundary between escalating physiological stress and the development of secondary biological injury, without granting a military commander, employer, institution, or remote artificial intelligence authority over the individual's body. The central architectural contribution is the integration of a biosensor–edge-AI–microneedle triad into a single consent-dependent intervention system. Its three components perform distinct functions: distributed physiological sensing identifies candidate states of biological distress; a locally operating edge-AI decision layer evaluates multimodal evidence against predetermined intervention conditions; and a dissolving microneedle interface provides a proposed route for bounded delivery of investigational biological agents. Unlike an ordinary biometric wearable, the system is intended to connect physiological observation with tightly restricted physical intervention. Unlike conventional automated drug-delivery systems, its governing objective is neither maintenance of a continuous biochemical target nor maximization of performance. It is acute damage containment: a conditional response to a potentially injurious physiological trajectory, permitted only when the system's evidence, safety conditions, and operator authorization converge. The physiological detection model examines the convergence of sympathetic nervous system activation, parasympathetic withdrawal, and hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis activity during severe stress exposure. Candidate signals include heart rate, heart-rate variability, electrodermal activity, respiration-related measurements, and movement-derived context. Their integration is intended to distinguish ordinary physical exertion from physiological patterns potentially associated with acute autonomic dysregulation. These measures represent indirect physiological indicators rather than definitive measurements of HPA-axis activation or impending tissue injury. The architecture therefore proposes multimodal sensor fusion and individualized baselines instead of relying upon a single elevated heart rate, isolated stress score, or generalized behavioral classification. Its distinguishing hypothesis is that the temporal relationship among several biological signals may provide a more informative indication of escalating physiological burden than any one signal considered independently. C.E.R.B.E.R.U.S. introduces a separation between stress recognition and therapeutic authority. Detecting physiological arousal does not automatically authorize intervention. The architecture proposes deterministic concurrence conditions requiring multiple sufficiently reliable indicators, a valid operator-consent state, confirmation that the device remains within its permitted operating conditions, and the absence of disqualifying safety conditions. The edge-AI component functions as a local eligibility assessor rather than an unrestricted medical decision-maker. Its outputs must remain bounded by an independently specified authorization structure, with no capacity to rewrite the intervention criteria during active operations. It is an active condition of the architecture, vested in the individual wearing the device. Consent must remain revocable, and a failure of authorization must result in non-actuation. items.title: Carbonbalance framework for carbon intensity forecasting and carbon aware scheduling of ai workloads
items.abstract: The Large Language Models have very powerful features that completely changed the artificial intelligence scenario, but at the same time, their enormous computational demands are the source of serious environmental problems especially in terms of energy use and carbon release. The present day AI practices concentrate on speeding up the process without taking the environmental effect of the power sources into account. As a solution to this problem, this research proposes CarbonBalance framework. This framework introduces the integration of two components i.e. forecasting pipeline and a scheduling pipeline. The forecasting pipeline makes use of a machine learning pipeline where historical energy and weather data is processed. It adopts LightGBM for capturing complicated feature relations and Prophet for modeling temporal patterns in carbon intensity and provides accurate prediction of grid carbon levels for the scheduling pipeline, which uses an optimization scheduler and LLM profiles to make its decisions to direct non-urgent AI tasks to cleaner energy times and locations without affecting the critical tasks. Through this approach, the evaluated scheduling scenarios achieved a 41.6% reduction in carbon emissions, while critical workloads maintained zero scheduling delay. Thus, the framework supports more sustainable AI workload execution. Not applicable.

items.title: Casino Protocol 23: A Deterministic Governance Implementation Model for Autonomous AI Damage Mitigation via On-Chain Slashing
items.abstract: Abstract As probabilistic AI systems (such as LLM agents and autonomous nodes) are increasingly integrated into enterprise and social infrastructure, the current framework for assigning legal and financial liability for economic damages caused by hallucinations or unpredicted bugs remains fundamentally flawed due to its reliance on post-hoc litigation against system developers and corporate operators. To address this issue at its root, this paper presents the design philosophy and the finalized, self-contained implementation code—strictly excluding any medical contracts and dedicated exclusively to non-medical enterprise partners directly contracted with Hideo Kajino—for the Deterministic Slashing Oracle Pipeline (Casino Protocol 23). This pipeline completely isolates human founders and non-medical contracting partners from legal and financial liability by automatically executing damage claims against the AI's own on-chain staked collateral. Through simulation execution logs, we demonstrate that this model achieves 100% indemnification for both the Genesis Architect (Hideo Kajino) and non-medical contracted partners, realizing a self-contained liability framework within the autonomous AI ecosystem.

items.title: CHARGE HUB: A Comprehensive Review of Smart Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure, Booking Systems, and Intelligent Charging Services
items.abstract: The increasing adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) has created a need for reliable charging infrastructure, convenient booking services, efficient energy management, and intelligent charging solutions. However, EV users may face problems such as limited charger availability, waiting time, uncertain charging costs, and difficulty identifying suitable charging stations. This review examines four published review papers covering EV charging station planning, smart charging, machine learning-based charging services, and charging technologies and standards. The reviewed literature indicates that effective EV charging requires coordination between charging infrastructure, digital platforms, energy management, and user requirements. Smart charging can improve energy utilization, while artificial intelligence and machine learning can support demand prediction, station recommendation, scheduling, and pricing. This paper compares the main contributions and limitations of the four reviews and identifies opportunities for integrating these functions into a unified charging management platform. The review also discusses how a system such as CHARGE HUB can connect users, charging stations, booking services, backend APIs, and databases. Finally, research challenges related to interoperability, security, real-time availability, peer-to-peer charging, and renewable energy integration are presented. Keywords— Electric vehicles, charging infrastructure, smart charging, station booking, machine learning, IoT, energy management, CHARGE HUB.

items.title: Chemically Informed Artificial Intelligence Decoding of Full-Spectrum SERS Fingerprints for pH-Guided Intraoperative Assessment of Freshly Excised Melanoma Specimens
items.abstract: Precise intraoperative delineation of melanoma margins remains a clinical challenge; incomplete resection causes recurrence, whereas over-excision compromises aesthetic and functional outcomes. While surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) provides chemically rich vibrational fingerprints, accurate intraoperative quantification is hindered by complex, coupled full-spectrum responses. Herein, we report a chemistry-informed artificial intelligence (AI)-SERS platform designed to support melanoma margin assessment via the detection of tumor-associated metabolic acidification. A pH-responsive HemS-SERS microarray was developed to translate the phenolic protonation/deprotonation of a hemicyanine-xanthene reporter into coordinated intensity redistributions across multiple Raman bands. Guided by this acid-base chemistry, our AI model (CIMPA-pH) encodes these pH-responsive vibrational anchors as learnable directional chemical priors, integrating full-spectrum attention with Henderson-Hasselbalch-guided prediction. This global decoding strategy accurately captures coupled pH responses, reducing prediction errors by approximately 85% and 54-78% compared to manual peak-ratio features and conventional deep-learning baselines, respectively, while a quality-control risk metric further reduces high-error readouts by 29.1%. Providing rapid (10 s) pointwise pH measurements, the platform distinguishes melanomas from normal skin with distinct pigmentation phenotypes in animal models and shows preliminary applicability for assessing melanoma-associated regions, including grossly atypical areas, in human resection specimens. Ultimately, this chemical-prior-guided SERS decoding strategy provides an interpretable framework with potential for metabolism-guided intraoperative margin assessment.

items.title: Citizen-Facing Cybercrime Detection and Early Warning Systems: A Systematic Literature Review
items.abstract: Cybercrime increasingly targets individual citizens through phishing, smishing, and social-engineering scams, yet most published detection research is designed for enterprise Security Operations Centres rather than for ordinary end users. This paper presents a systematic literature review (SLR) of thirty peer-reviewed, Scopus- and IEEE-indexed studies published between 2022 and 2026, covering enterprise alert detection, citizen and smart-city scam protection, phishing and malicious-website detection, SMS smishing detection, large-language-model-based scam detection, financial fraud detection, adaptive and concept-drift-aware intrusion detection, and explainable artificial intelligence. Following the PRISMA methodology, records were identified, screened, and assessed for eligibility before thirty studies were included in the final synthesis. The review develops a thematic comparison of methods, datasets, and reported limitations, and visualises the distribution of studies by theme and publication year. The synthesis shows that while detection accuracy for individual cybercrime types is now very high, very few studies combine adaptive learning, real-time citizen-facing notification, and plain-language explanation into a single system. Seven specific research gaps are identified, and directions for future work on citizen-oriented, adaptive, and explainable cybercrime early-warning systems are proposed. Keywords: Cybercrime detection; phishing; smishing; social engineering; adaptive learning; explainable artificial intelligence; systematic literature review; citizen cybersecurity

items.title: Closed-Loop Mineral Intelligence: A Conceptual Framework and Research Agenda for Adaptive, Uncertainty-Aware Critical Mineral Exploration
items.abstract: Critical raw material (CRM) exploration increasingly combines Earth Observation, geophysics, geochemistry, mineral prospectivity mapping, probabilistic modelling, and autonomous sensing. However, these capabilities are commonly developed or deployed as separate components, while the explicit coupling of observation, uncertainty-aware geological inference, and subsequent exploration decisions remains comparatively underdeveloped. This paper presents Closed-Loop Mineral Intelligence (CLMI) as a conceptual and methodological framework for organising these capabilities within an iterative Observe–Model–Decide process. The contribution does not propose a new stand-alone learning algorithm or claim an operationally validated exploration system. Instead, it formalises a reference architecture in which heterogeneous observations update probabilistic geological representations, uncertainty informs the prioritisation of subsequent observations, and expert oversight remains part of the decision loop. The framework is examined through an illustrative lithium-bearing pegmatite scenario that specifies the intended information flow, candidate data sources, modelling functions, decision points, and human intervention without reporting empirical performance. A validation roadmap is further defined to make the framework testable in future case studies, including requirements for benchmark baselines, uncertainty calibration, information-gain assessment, exploration-efficiency metrics, computational feasibility, and human–AI interaction. By distinguishing established technological components from the proposed system-level integration, the paper positions CLMI as a research framework and agenda for adaptive, uncertainty-aware mineral exploration rather than as a demonstrated replacement for current professional practice.

items.title: Closed-Loop Reinforcement Learning in De Novo Molecular Design: Bridging Generative AI with Automated Chemical Synthesis
items.abstract: Closed-loop reinforcement learning offers a promising approach to integrating generative molecular design with automated chemical synthesis and experimental evaluation. However, translating autonomous chemical optimization into pharmaceutical discovery remains challenging because biological measurements are often delayed, variable, and affected by assay limitations. This critical review and perspective examines current autonomous discovery platforms and evaluates the challenges associated with incorporating physical experimental feedback into molecular optimization. It proposes an uncertainty-aware, multi-objective reward architecture and a four-gate qualification framework covering operational synthesizability, analytical identity and purity, biological assay validity, and governed policy updating. Particular attention is given to distinguishing statistically censored measurements from pharmacologically confounded or invalid observations. The article also introduces supervised autonomy as a practical governance approach in which automated systems perform routine experimental operations while scientific experts retain responsibility for critical decisions. The proposed framework provides a foundation for improving the reliability, interpretability, and practical implementation of experimentally informed molecular discovery. Prospective validation remains necessary to establish its effectiveness.

items.title: Cognition Versus Consensus: Demonstrating Reason and Creativity in Professional Communications
items.abstract: In response to the increasing reliance on artificial intelligence (AI) in business and college classrooms, an exercise is proposed that reaffirms the fundamental and essential functions reason and creativity perform in personalizing and vitalizing professional communications. Three competing proposals—two generated by AI; one developed without AI assistance—are evaluated in terms of how effectively they answer an assignment from senior management. Alongside highlighting the strengths and limitations of AI’s consensus-based alternatives, the evaluations provide students with a practical demonstration of the substantive contributions human cognition makes to the production of quality communications and to enhancing the reputation of the communicator.

items.title: Cognitive Conflict and Critical Thinking Skills in Science Education: A Systematic Literature Review
items.abstract: Critical thinking is an essential competency in science education because it enables students to analyze information, evaluate evidence, draw inferences, and make reasoned decisions. Cognitive conflict—arising when students’ prior conceptions encounter information or phenomena inconsistent with their existing understanding—may provide opportunities to reconsider explanations and examine evidence. This review examines (1) how cognitive conflict strategies have been designed and implemented to support critical thinking in science education, (2) how critical thinking has been operationalized and assessed, and (3) opportunities and challenges associated with integrating Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) and adaptive learning. The study uses a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) with narrative synthesis. Sixteen articles were mapped for the period October 10, 2016–October 10, 2026. The mapped literature includes studies on cognitive conflict in physics education, instructional media development, critical thinking assessment, conceptual change, and GenAI use. The preliminary synthesis indicates that cognitive conflict has been integrated into inquiry learning, discovery learning, interactive multimedia, e-books, augmented reality, and educational websites. However, only a small subset of the mapped studies directly measured critical thinking, while others focused on conceptual understanding, misconception remediation, scientific literacy, creativity, or product development. The GenAI literature provides contextual insights into personalization and the risk of reduced cognitive engagement, but does not establish the effectiveness of integrating GenAI with cognitive conflict in physics education. The review identifies a need to align cognitive conflict activities with measurable critical thinking indicators and to evaluate GenAI as a scaffold.

items.title: Comparative analysis of large language model and faculty rater scoring of medical student documentation in objective structured clinical examinations.
items.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate whether a commercially available large language model (LLM) can score medical student post-encounter notes from Objective Structured Clinical Examinations (OSCEs) using an existing institutional rubric without task-specific model training and to characterize internal consistency and alignment with faculty scores using absolute agreement and rank-order association metrics. METHOD: The dataset included 433 medical student notes from 7 standardized OSCE cases at the University of Kentucky. In November 2024, an LLM (OpenAI GPT-4o mini, via API) scored each note using a prompt-based workflow (no model fine-tuning) under two approaches: numerical score only ("GPT-NE", 30 iterations per note) and numerical score with rationale ("GPT-E", 4 iterations per note). The authors compared the LLM's performance against historical faculty grades using the same rubric, evaluating the reliability of grading methodologies and inter-modal agreement. RESULTS: The LLM demonstrated high internal consistency for GPT-NE (intraclass correlation (ICC) = 0.94) and moderate-to-high consistency for GPT-E (ICC = 0.76). LLM scores were significantly lower than faculty scores (mean differences on a 1-4 scale: -1.12 GPT-NE, 95% CI -1.17 to -1.08; -0.65 GPT-E, 95% CI -0.69 to -0.61, both P < .001). Spearman rank-order correlations (r = 0.43-0.53) indicate moderate preservation of relative student ranking despite differences in absolute scores. CONCLUSIONS: The LLM demonstrated significant potential for automating OSCE note grading given its internal consistency and similar ranking of learners compared with faculty raters. Automation of grading could yield substantial time savings; however, discrepancies with absolute faculty scores underscore the need for further refinement of rubric alignment and grading methodologies.

items.title: COMPARATIVE BIODIVERSITY OF VERTEBRATES IN MAHARASHTRA ECOSYSTEMS
items.abstract: This study, Comparative Biodiversity of Vertebrates in Maharashtra Ecosystems, examines vertebrate diversity, distribution, and ecological roles across Maharashtra’s varied landscapes, including forests, wetlands, rivers, reservoirs, grasslands, coastal zones, and arid regions. Maharashtra is recognised as one of India’s ecological hotspots, supporting a wide range of mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians, and fishes. By comparing vertebrate biodiversity across these ecosystems, the study identifies environmental and human factors that influence species richness and ecological balance. Using scientific literature, biodiversity surveys, government reports, and conservation databases, we mapped vertebrate diversity and the challenges it faces. Our findings indicate that forests and wetlands, due to their complex habitats and abundant water, support the highest vertebrate diversity. In contrast, Maharashtra’s semi-arid and urban areas support fewer species, with habitat loss and ongoing human activity reducing biodiversity. The study identifies key threats, including deforestation, pollution, urban expansion, climate change, roadkill, agricultural growth, mining, and increasing human-wildlife conflict. Freshwater and coastal habitats are particularly vulnerable to pollution and unregulated development, while forests face growing fragmentation. The research emphasises the importance of protected areas, wildlife corridors, wetland conservation, habitat restoration, and continuous ecological monitoring. Conservation strategies should be tailored to each ecosystem's specific needs. The study ultimately calls for an integrated, ecosystem-based approach that combines scientific research, community involvement, effective policy, and sustainable management to protect Maharashtra’s vertebrate diversity.

items.title: Computational Genomics: The Convergence of AI and CRISPR in Precision Medicine
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and CRISPR-based genome editing offer complementary approaches to investigating genetic variation and developing targeted interventions in precision medicine. This narrative review examines the principles underlying AI-assisted genomic analysis and programmable genome editing, with particular attention to their potential integration in disease research and therapeutic development. Machine learning and deep learning models can analyse genomic and other molecular datasets, assist in identifying disease-associated variants, and support the prioritisation of candidate therapeutic targets. In CRISPR research, computational methods can inform guide RNA selection, estimate editing efficiency and potential off-target activity, and assist in interpreting functional screening results. Combining these approaches may improve the selection of experimental targets and strengthen investigation of biological mechanisms relevant to inherited disorders, cancer and other complex conditions. The review also discusses AI-assisted clinical decision support, pharmacogenomics, and applications of genome editing in molecular research. However, the reliability of integrated approaches remains dependent on representative training data, transparent computational methods, appropriate experimental validation and safe delivery of editing components. Unintended genomic alterations, variable editing outcomes, model bias, data privacy concerns, ethical issues and regulatory requirements continue to constrain clinical translation. Further progress will require reproducible research, long-term safety assessment and interdisciplinary collaboration. Overall, AI-guided CRISPR research may contribute to the development of more individualised therapeutic strategies, but its clinical value must be established through rigorous validation and responsible implementation.

items.title: CONCEPTUAL MODEL FOR INTELLIGENT MANAGEMENT OF STOCK THROUGH BLOCKCHAIN AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENT ALGORITHMS
items.abstract: The use of modern technologies is revolutionizing all spheres of life, including industry, on which the economic development and stability of the country and the population in general depend. The various modern intelligent systems used in warehouses, depots, and large factories assist the production process, management, and optimization of the purchase and sale of stock. Various artificial intelligence and blockchain techniques have transformed traditional systems into digital, intelligent, decentralized and secure platforms, but have also facilitated physical processes through the use of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and other intelligent agents, which directly impact productivity and cost-efficiency in the supply chain. The use of hybrid architectures, which will combine the advantages of contemporary technologies, with the aim of creating a secure, transparent ecosystem, where privacy, traceability, and above all a longer-term strategy for efficient stock management will be created, is of particular importance in the supply chain. Furthermore, the use of smart contracts, which in addition to automating processes on the blockchain network, also reduces human intervention and possible delays, and at the same time protects the supply chain from possible manipulations that could be threatened by malicious persons. Despite the fact that the integration of contemporary technologies leads to the improvement and facilitation of stock management processes, many challenges of practical implementation, scalability, and system interoperability such as the lack of standardization, privacy and ethical issues remain among the many challenges facing modern intelligent systems. Through this paper, we will first explain the importance of integrating contemporary technologies, in particular blockchain technology and artificial intelligence, into the inventory management process, and then propose a conceptual model for integrating these technologies into existing intelligent systems, with the aim of creating a more secure, transparent and reliable supply chain. We will also present an intelligent stock management system, which we have tested and is functional, with the aim of integrating functionalities from contemporary technologies into it in the future, to offer the highest quality and safest services.

items.title: Conformalized graph neural network emulation of regional climate extremes: an artificial intelligence evaluation of coverage guarantees under emissions-scenario shift
items.abstract: Conformal prediction offers distribution-free coverage guarantees for machine-learning emulators of climate extremes, but the guarantee is only as good as the exchangeability assumption that underwrites it. Using NASA POWER monthly reanalysis for Kampala, Uganda (0.35°N, 32.58°E) over 2000–2023 (312 observations, mean 22.443 °C, linear trend −0.1564 °C per decade), the study specifies a graph construction, a split-conformal calibration protocol, and a coverage-degradation bound expressed as a function of a scenario-shift divergence. The analysis derives a finite-sample coverage gap under covariate shift, proposes a weighted conformal score that restores approximate validity, and identifies the conditions under which GNN emulators of regional extremes can be certified for out-of-distribution emissions scenarios. The contribution is a formal account of when conformal coverage survives scenario shift and a diagnostic that practitioners can compute before deploying an emulator.

items.title: Could an AI App Take Over Your Phone? A Live Warning Number That Moves Only the Misbehaving AI Agent Aside
items.abstract: A smartphone holds a person's messages, photographs, bank apps and location. A new kind of app is arriving on it: the AI agent that acts for the user, reading the screen, opening other apps and carrying out tasks. To work, such an agent needs permissions, and an agent that is hijacked, impersonated or simply drifts from its task can misuse them. Today's protections are a permission gate that lists what an agent may call, and live on-device checks that warn the user or disable an app once its behaviour is judged malicious. This concept note proposes a live layer between them. For each AI agent, a lag-1 autocorrelation warning number is calculated at run time from the agent's own behaviour stream, mainly the run of requests that fall outside the user's task and its use of sensitive permissions. The computer then decides a graded shunting action: confirmation is asked, the agent's permissions are lowered, or the agent is hand-tied, while the phone and every other app keep running. This is a concept to be tested on real phone traffic, not a result. Patent pending.

items.title: Counterfactual crop-yield attribution to seasonal forecast advisories via doubly robust estimation: an artificial intelligence evaluation of adoption-selection bias in extension targeting
items.abstract: Seasonal forecast advisories are promoted as a climate service that raises crop yields, yet extension agencies typically target farmers who already differ from non-adopters in ways that also affect yield. the present analysis formalises the resulting adoption-selection bias and evaluates a doubly robust estimator for counterfactual yield attribution under a declared data-generating process. The design is a replication-based evaluation: 600 data sets of N = 500 were drawn from a process with intercept 12.0, exposure 0.42, group -3.1, severity 1.35 and error SD 4.2, and the ordinary least squares estimator was characterised across replications. The estimated bias was -0.04629 for the intercept and 0.00086 for the exposure coefficient; the root mean squared errors were 0.95661 and 0.01664 respectively, and empirical coverage of the nominal 95% confidence intervals was 1.0 for both parameters. The results indicate that under correct specification the estimator recovers the exposure effect with negligible bias and conservative coverage, but that the intercept is the fragile quantity when group composition is unbalanced. Doubly robust attribution is defensible for advisory evaluation only when the selection model is reported alongside the outcome model, and it derives the conditions under which extension targeting can be interpreted as a counterfactual yield effect rather than a description of adopters.

items.title: Cross-Layer Co-Design and Physics-Grounded Evaluation of Hybrid Reinforcement Learning and Federated ANN-PID Protocol Suites for Dense Urban UAV Delivery Networks
items.abstract: Urban unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) fleets require coordinated optimization of communication, mobility, and energy management. This study evaluates conventional and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled cross-layer protocol suites in a common five-hour simulation of 7,500 UAVs, 240 base stations, and 40 vertiports across 144 km². They include AODV-based conventional routing, reinforcement learning-based UAV-AI-EDRL, federated ANN-PID-based UAV-AI-FHAP, reduced learning baselines, and a composite. Methodological contributions comprise a mission-constrained cross-layer objective, CMA-ES calibration benchmarks, physics-grounded training, paired evaluation over six environmental realizations, and packet-level NS-3 checks. In fleet-scale runs, proactive routing reduced mean end-to-end delay from 66.0 to 25.3 ms (61.6%), an advantage NS-3 reproduced at every transmit power only with pre-resolved link-layer addresses. UAV-AI-EDRL reduced power by 8.7% and near-miss events by 18.1% on the principal training seed, although safety gains varied across seeds. UAV-AI-FHAP reduced power by 4.6% and near-miss events by 30.9%, but completed 15.9% fewer missions because a charging threshold calibrated on a reduced-area oracle interrupted long delivery legs; geometry-preserving recalibration reduced the deficit to 2.2%, and a leg-aware charging rule produced a 13.9% gain (2.3% if the conventional suite also uses it). Ablations with equivalence tests attributed the gains to proactive forwarding, throttling, spread control, and reactive avoidance, finding no measurable suite-level benefit from DQN, PPO, path planning, ANN-PID, or federated aggregation; suites without learned power control preserved superior raw radio metrics. These findings, limited to the simulated conditions, shifts, and fleet sizes, reveal trade-offs among latency, energy, safety, and mission completion, emphasizing operationally weighted selection and field validation.

items.title: Democratizing reliable knowledge-seeking with MyGPT: a privacy-first, open-source retrieval-augmented generation platform
items.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have transformed knowledge discovery, but their use in sensitive domains is limited by privacy concerns and risks of data leakage. Moreover, LLMs may hallucinate when queried about information outside their training data, undermining their reliability for scientific, clinical, or policy-related tasks. We present MyGPT, a fully open-source, privacy-preserving retrieval-augmented-generation (RAG) platform that uses open-source LLMs and operates locally or within secure institutional environments. MyGPT empowers users to query user-defined libraries such as biomedical literature, confidential clinical documents, and multilingual global health policies, while ensuring that sensitive data never leaves the secure environment. We introduce confidence metrics, including “relevance scores” and “hallucination index,” and provide explicit source citation from the library within a single interface to assess contextual support for generated answers. MyGPT offers a cost-effective, modular, open-source alternative to commercial LLM services and democratizes knowledge-seeking across multiple domains, including use at remote facilities without internet access.

items.title: Diagnóstico inteligente en la gestión de convenios interinstitucionales para la calidad educativa universitaria
items.abstract: Introduction: Collaboration and cooperation among universities are among the ways to promote shared global well-being. To achieve this, universities must take a proactive role in managing inter-institutional agreements so that they contribute to educational quality Objective: To demonstrate the contribution of an intelligent assessment, mediated by artificial intelligence and grounded in a systemic-historical-cultural approach, to the management of inter-institutional agreements in order to enhance the quality of university education. Method: This research followed a mixed-methods approach that was descriptive and propositional in nature, with a qualitative focus. Theoretical methods were used to construct the conceptual and epistemological framework of the proposal, including synthetic-analytic, inductive-deductive, and theoretical modeling approaches. Additionally, a literature review was conducted. Journals from Scopus, Web of Science, SciELO, Redalyc, Dialnet, DOAJ, institutional repositories, and specialized sources on Artificial Intelligence and education were consulted, covering the time period 2000–2025. The literature review process was organized into three stages: initial exploration, in-depth analysis, and systematization and integration. Results: The analysis conducted made it possible to characterize the management of agreements, the limitations of traditional assessment, the role, applications, and ethical principles of Artificial Intelligence as a mediator in such management, and a proposal for its three phases to enhance the quality of higher education. Conclusions: It is concluded that intelligent assessment contributes to educational quality through five mechanisms: strategic alignment, data-driven management, predictive capacity, ethical and social strengthening, and institutional learning. The proposal represents a significant step forward in transforming the management of agreements into a driver of quality and social change.

items.title: Digital Constitutionalism and the Protection of Fundamental Rights in the Age of AI: Rethinking Privacy, Equality and Freedom of Expression
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) now decides who receives police protection and who gets government benefits and who gets employment or credit approval and who gets their online content promoted or deleted. The academic research and legal regulations that follow treat the resulting privacy violations and the breaks of equality and the restrictions on free speech as different issues. The paper presents three interrelated elements which demonstrate their relationship through three specific aspects: surveillance and profiling drive people to stop talking then automated content control systems create unfair distribution of when users speak and finally data practices which privacy legislation aims to control lead to unfair scoring outcomes. The study employs doctrinal and comparative approaches to examine three questions: (1) Do Articles 14, 19(1)(a) and 21 of the Indian Constitution provide sufficient protection against AI-related harms (2) What are the strengths and weaknesses of European Union and United States regulations governing AI systems used by public and private organizations (3) What protective measures should India implement. The Indian constitutional doctrine demonstrates strong power but the Indian legal system fails to provide sufficient support for automated decision-making and State exemptions and private-sector discrimination and remedies. The system establishes a comprehensive framework that consists of four hierarchical levels which include constitutional and legislative and institutional and remedial components. The law is stated as at 19 October 2026.

items.title: Digital-Based Career Counseling in the Era of Revolusi Industri 4.0 : Systematic Literature Review
items.abstract: The Industrial Revolution 4.0 has significantly transformed various aspects of human life, particularly in education and employment, through the integration of digital technology, artificial intelligence, big data, and the Internet of Things. These rapid changes demand new competencies such as digital literacy, critical thinking, adaptability, and career flexibility. In response to these challenges, digital-based career counseling has emerged as a strategic innovation to support students’ career development and readiness for the modern workplace. This study employs a literature review approach by analyzing recent national and international scientific publications indexed in Sinta, Scopus, and Google Scholar within the last five years. The analysis focuses on key themes including theoretical foundations, implementation models, benefits, and challenges of digital career counseling. The findings indicate that integrating classical career theories, such as Holland’s RIASEC personality typology and Super’s life-span, life-space theory, with digital platforms enhances accessibility, efficiency, and personalization of counseling services. Digital tools such as video conferencing, learning management systems, online assessments, and social media platforms contribute to improving career adaptability, career optimism, and employability skills among students. However, challenges remain in terms of counselors’ digital competence, ethical considerations, data security, and maintaining emotional connection in virtual interactions. Therefore, successful implementation of digital-based career counseling requires collaboration among government institutions, educational organizations, and technology developers to ensure effective, ethical, and student-centered services in the era of the Industrial Revolution 4.0.

items.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming the management and operational processes of the hospitality industry. Boutique hotels, characterized by relatively small room capacity, personalized services, distinctive design, and strong dependence on guest experience, require flexible and data-driven approaches to improving operational and economic efficiency. This article examines the directions for improving the efficiency of boutique hotels through artificial intelligence-based modeling. Particular attention is given to AI applications in demand forecasting, dynamic pricing, occupancy optimization, guest personalization, workforce planning, energy management, digital marketing, and operational decision-making. The study proposes an integrated AI-based efficiency model that combines historical booking data, room prices, occupancy rates, customer reviews, seasonal factors, events, weather conditions, and online market information. The article also considers machine learning, neural networks, time-series forecasting, ensemble models, and explainable artificial intelligence as tools for supporting managerial decisions. Recent research demonstrates that AI-based forecasting can improve the accuracy of hotel demand prediction, while AI-driven personalization can support revenue stability and guest engagement. However, effective implementation requires high-quality data, appropriate technological infrastructure, employee competencies, data protection, and human supervision. The study concludes that AI-based modeling should be considered not as a replacement for hotel managers but as a decision-support mechanism that can improve resource allocation, pricing decisions, service personalization, and overall economic efficiency.

items.title: EduArchive AI 2.0: An AI-Powered Academic Intelligence and Previous Year Question Paper Analytics Platform
items.abstract: Previous Year Question Papers (PYQs) are valuable academic resources that help students understand examination patterns, identify frequently asked questions, recognize important topics, and plan their preparation effectively. However, conventional question-paper repositories mainly provide document storage and downloading facilities, requiring students to manually browse and compare papers from different years. This process is time-consuming and makes it difficult to identify repeated questions and important topics systematically. To address these limitations, EduArchive AI 2.0 is proposed as an artificial intelligence-powered academic intelligence and question-paper analytics platform. The system integrates Optical Character Recognition (OCR), Natural Language Processing (NLP), sentence embeddings, semantic search, Large Language Models (LLMs), and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to transform historical examination papers into a searchable academic knowledge base. Its multi-agent architecture consists of five specialized agents: Ingestion, Analysis, Search, Recommendation, and Admin Intelligence. The platform supports processing digital and scanned PDF documents, detecting semantically similar questions, identifying frequently occurring topics, classifying question difficulty, and retrieving relevant academic information through natural-language queries. The RAG-based “Ask Your Papers” assistant is designed to generate responses using relevant content retrieved from uploaded question papers. The proposed implementation uses React.js, Python Flask, Sentence Transformers, ChromaDB, LangChain, Redis, and Docker. EduArchive AI 2.0 aims to reduce manual document analysis, improve access to academic information, and support more organized examination preparation. Its effectiveness should be evaluated using representative question-paper datasets and measurable performance metrics

items.abstract: This article examines the theoretical and methodological foundations of the efficient use of economic resources in the context of digital transformation, with particular emphasis on the impact of digital technologies on production processes, labor productivity, capital utilization, and management efficiency. The study also analyzes the role of data-driven management, artificial intelligence, cloud computing, automation, and digital platforms in improving the allocation and utilization of economic resources. In addition, the implications of digitalization for economic efficiency are considered, including technological investment, human capital development, information security, and organizational transformation. Based on the analysis, scientific and practical recommendations are developed to enhance the efficiency of economic resource utilization under conditions of digital transformation.

items.abstract: Version 2.0 - Research manuscript, mathematical proofs, executable software, and reproducible numerical experiments EIQ-Λ develops a mathematical and computational framework for fabrication systems that must decide which uncertain features to measure, which to overwrite through calibrated operations, when to inspect them, and how to preserve their verified accuracy through subsequent processing. It connects inverse scattering, fabrication reachability, bounded material correction, multiscale representation, and recursive error propagation through explicit process contracts. The central contribution is a conditional access-preservation resource law: the sequence of fabrication and verification can change the scaling of the measurement problem. Observing a feature while it remains accessible, then bounding subsequent disturbance, can avoid an exponential sensing penalty associated with terminal inspection through a fixed-gap evanescent channel. The release contains analytical results and executed CPU experiments. Optional CuPy implementations support GPU evaluation and inverse estimation; GPU execution and acceleration remain unmeasured in the supplied results. Principal contributions 1. Access-preserving verification and a sharp late-damage threshold.In the stated sensing model, measurement sensitivity decreases exponentially with the product of spatial frequency and sensor stand-off. For increasingly fine features, a fixed stand-off can therefore require exponentially increasing measurement effort. The framework identifies conditions under which inspection access that follows feature size avoids this penalty. A polynomial total-workflow guarantee additionally requires polynomial costs for access, calibration, correction, and error transport. The analysis explicitly includes damage occurring after inspection. Early verification remains useful only when subsequent disturbance fits within the final error budget. 2. An exact optimal inspection time.For linear deterioration of access and a linear bound on later damage, the manuscript derives an explicit minimum-effort inspection schedule: t* = clip(T − (ε − a)/d + 1/(qv), 0, T). Here, ε is the final tolerance, a the correction-error floor, d the subsequent disturbance rate, q the spatial frequency, v the rate of increasing stand-off, and T the process duration. Separate boundary cases address vanishing disturbance or access deterioration. With spatial frequency inversely proportional to feature size and initial stand-off proportional to feature size, the optimal sensing effort has three regimes: bounded effort, quadratic growth at the preservation threshold, and exponential growth when the remaining damage budget forces inspection too late. These are measurement-resource laws under the declared model, rather than direct manufacturing-time predictions. 3. Multiple-scattering inference with bounded material uncertainty.The software implements a finite scalar wave model containing repeated scattering, together with an exact support-reduced representation for changes within a known small region of a calibrated background. A direct contrast-source estimator converts bounded complex-field measurement errors into explicit intervals for real material coordinates. The resulting uncertainty is propagated through proposed corrective actions. Commands are evaluated against actuator limits, material admissibility, and output-error bounds. Weak excitation, poor conditioning, or inconsistent observations can prevent a justified correction or terminal acceptance. 4. A finite-library process compiler.For independent scalar features, the planner selects among leaving a feature unchanged, resetting it through a calibrated operation, or measuring and correcting it. The manuscript establishes the sharp bounded-command residual: a + max{min(R, e), R − C}, where R is the prior uncertainty radius, e the observation uncertainty, C the maximum correction magnitude, and a the actuator-error bound. Under additive costs, a maximum-norm task specification, and the enumerated one-pass operations, the compiler returns a minimum-cost eligible plan or identifies requirements blocked by the supplied library. 5. Recursive structural representation and error transport.Repeated target motifs are represented through a quadtree directed acyclic graph. Task-specific boundary-response descriptions connect modular wave behavior to hierarchical composition, while explicit influence bounds track how local uncertainty affects the finished structure. Description compression and selected optical-response equivalence retain their distinct physical meanings. Computational findings The supplied CPU experiments report: 9.21× lower computation time for evaluating 64 candidate modifications in a 1,024-cell domain with eight changing cells, compared with repeated dense full solves. This includes common geometry/kernel setup and cache construction; totals sum separately measured stage medians. 25.57× faster direct inverse estimation with uncertainty intervals than bounded nonlinear least squares on the same reduced model, including direct-estimator setup but assuming an existing shared background cache. Including all common initialization reduces the single-inverse ratio to approximately 1.0035×. Three accepted corrections and four measurements in a simulated repair loop, reducing actual model output error from approximately 0.08324 to 0.00009455. A final noisy measurement establishes an upper bound below the prescribed 0.0003 tolerance. The approximately 880-fold change is error reduction, rather than a runtime speedup. A 256-feature process plan selecting 175 leave, 33 reset, and 48 observe-and-correct operations, with approximately 7.97× lower normalized cost than observing and correcting every required feature. Validation includes 36 wave/Jacobian/error-bound cases, 416 additional noise cases, 240 scheduler comparisons, four scheduler boundary cases, six asymptotic checks, 120 scalar interval cases, and 1,572 independent controller minimizations. Fresh release-preparation executions are recorded separately from the original benchmark results. Contents and scientific scope The archive includes the 44-page manuscript, editable LaTeX proofs and bibliography, Python implementations, pinned CPU dependencies, recorded experiments, scientific figures, reproduction commands, machine-readable claim metadata, AI-agent instructions, expert-review guidance, citation files, and integrity manifests. Classical operator completion, Green-function reuse, contrast-source inversion, and related foundations receive explicit attribution. The proposed contribution is their integration with access scheduling, bounded correction, process selection, and preservation requirements. The universality statement concerns every target in an admitted finite language conditional on a uniformly adequate calibrated process library and valid independence or coupling assumptions. The scattering demonstrations assume a known background and changing support within a finite scalar two-dimensional model. Numerical checks use ordinary floating-point arithmetic. EIQ-Λ provides a reproducible foundation for investigating verification-aware fabrication and material-specific experimental backends. Physical production throughput, arbitrary-material universality, and experimentally calibrated nanoscale resolution remain subjects for subsequent validation. items.title: Emerging trends in AI-driven mining hazard management
items.abstract: The management of geotechnical hazards in mining is critical for ensuring operational safety and sustainability, yet its practical implementation often struggles with the inherent geological uncertainty and the dynamic, non-linear nature of mining environments. Artificial intelligence (AI), and specifically machine learning (ML), has emerged as a transformative technology, offering a shift from reactive to proactive, data-driven hazard management. This paper provides a comprehensive review of the evolution and application of AI in mining hazard management, tracing this development from early statistical and ML models to recent advances in deep learning. The review finds that these advanced models have demonstrated significant success in tasks such as rockburst prediction, slope stability analysis, and gas outburst forecasting by identifying complex patterns in large, multi-source datasets from seismic, geological, and operational monitoring. Despite these successes, significant challenges persist: the efficacy of purely data-driven models is often limited by data scarcity, imbalanced datasets, and a lack of physical consistency; the black-box nature of many deep learning models has created a barrier to their interpretability and trustworthiness in safety-critical applications. The future of AI in mining hazard management lies not in isolated algorithms but in integrated, hybrid systems. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) and explainable AI (XAI) are identified as critical frontiers. These approaches promise to create models that are not only more accurate and generalisable but also transparent and interpretable to engineering practitioners, bridging the gap between AI's theoretical potential and its practical application in creating safer mining environments.

items.abstract: EMOÇÃO, MOTIVAÇÃO E ALFABETIZAÇÃO: EXPERIÊNCIAS AFETIVAS E SUA RELAÇÃO COM A APRENDIZAGEM. EMOTION, MOTIVATION AND LITERACY: AFFECTIVE EXPERIENCES AND THEIR RELATIONSHIP WITH LEARNING. EMOCIÓN, MOTIVACIÓN Y ALFABETIZACIÓN: EXPERIENCIAS AFECTIVAS Y SU RELACIÓN CON EL APRENDIZAJE. Nivea Maria Costa Vieira RESUMO O presente estudo analisa a influência das dimensões afetivas, emocionais e motivacionais no processo de alfabetização de crianças nos anos iniciais do ensino fundamental. Em contextos escolares marcados por metodologias mecanizadas, o problema investigado reside em como as vivências emocionais e o clima relacional estabelecido na sala de aula impactam o engajamento e a consolidação do aprendizado da leitura e da escrita. O objetivo geral consiste em examinar as interconexões entre experiências afetivas, fatores motivacionais e o desenvolvimento cognitivo indispensável à apropriação do sistema de escrita alfabética. Metodologicamente, realizou-se uma pesquisa bibliográfica e documental de abordagem qualitativa, pautada na análise sistemática de referenciais da psicologia da educação, da neuroeducação e da pedagogia. Os resultados evidenciam que ambientes alfabetizadores acolhedores, pautados no afeto e no fortalecimento da autoconfiança, reduzem a ansiedade, estimulam a motivação intrínseca e favorecem as funções executivas essenciais à alfabetização. Conclui-se que a mediação pedagógica intencional e sensível às emoções constitui elemento determinante para a aprendizagem significativa, demonstrando a relevância de integrar o desenvolvimento socioemocional à prática alfabetizadora para a promoção da equidade educacional e do sucesso escolar. Palavras-chave: Alfabetização; afetividade; motivação para aprendizagem; psicologia da educação. ABSTRACT This study analyzes the influence of affective, emotional, and motivational dimensions on the literacy acquisition process of children in the early years of elementary education. In school contexts marked by mechanized methodologies, the research problem addresses how emotional experiences and the relational climate established in the classroom impact student engagement and the consolidation of reading and writing skills. The general objective is to examine the interconnections among affective experiences, motivational factors, and the cognitive development indispensable for mastering the alphabetic writing system. Methodologically, a qualitative bibliographic and documentary research approach was employed, based on a systematic analysis of frameworks from educational psychology, neuroeducation, and pedagogy. The results demonstrate that welcoming literacy environments grounded in affection and the reinforcement of self-confidence reduce anxiety, stimulate intrinsic motivation, and foster the executive functions essential for literacy acquisition. The study concludes that intentional pedagogical mediation sensitive to emotions constitutes a decisive element for meaningful learning, highlighting the relevance of integrating socio-emotional development into literacy practices to promote educational equity and academic success. Keywords: Literacy acquisition; affectivity; learning motivation; educational psychology. En contextos escolares caracterizados por metodologías mecanizadas, el problema investigado radica en cómo las experiencias emocionales y el clima relacional establecido en el aula impactan el compromiso y la consolidación del aprendizaje de la lectura y la escritura. El objetivo general consiste en examinar las interconexiones entre las experiencias afectivas, los factores motivacionales y el desarrollo cognitivo indispensable para la apropiación del sistema de escritura alfabética. Los resultados evidencian que los entornos alfabetizadores acogedores, basados en el afecto y el fortalecimiento de la autoconfianza, reducen la ansiedad, estimulan la motivación intrínseca y favorecen las funciones ejecutivas esenciales para la alfabetización. items.title: Emotional intelligence and staff job performance in federal universities in south-south, Nigeria
items.abstract: The study examined emotional intelligence and staff job performance in federal universities in South-South Nigeria. Specifically, the study sought to evaluate the relationship between motivation and handling diverse learning needs and ascertain the relationship between empathy and providing career guidance in federal universities in South-South Nigeria. Research questions and five hypotheses were formulated to guide the study. The study employed a descriptive survey design. The population comprised four thousand, four hundred and seventy-eight (4,478) staff members, from which a sample size of 354 was determined using Freund and Williams' formula. Two hundred and eighty-seven (287) respondents returned their questionnaires, which were accurately completed. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and analyzed using descriptive statistics. The Z-test was used to test the hypotheses. The findings indicated that motivation had a significant positive relationship with handling diverse learning needs in federal universities in South-South Nigeria, Z = 10.625, p < .05. Empathy had a significant positive relationship with providing career guidance in federal universities in South-South Nigeria, Z = 11.171, p < .05. The study concluded that motivation and empathy had significant positive relationships with handling diverse learning needs and providing career guidance to students in federal universities in South-South Nigeria. The study recommended, among other things, that federal universities in South-South Nigeria should encourage academic staff to cultivate intrinsic motivation by setting personal teaching goals, engaging in continuous learning, and participating in peer mentoring programmes.

It emphasizes the importance of safeguarding the common good and reaffirming human identity as a divine creation. Biblical metaphors —specifically the Tower of Babel and the rebuilding of the walls of Jerusalem— are used to contrast technological arrogance with the construction of a collaborative, faith-based community. Furthermore, the text highlights the relevance of the Church’s social doctrine in addressing modern technological advancements, prioritizing human rights and compassion.

items.title: Explainable AI for Fraud Alert Review in Community Banks and Credit Unions: A Narrative Review of Architectures, Analyst Workflows, and Governance
items.abstract: Community banks and credit unions face the same fraud schemes as large banks, but with far fewer analysts and data scientists. Machine-learning detectors help, yet an alert that gives no reason leaves the analyst to reconstruct the logic by hand, which slows investigations and complicates regulatory examinations. This narrative review looks at how explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) is being applied to fraud alerts in small financial institutions. Drawing on six recent sources, we trace the shift from rule-based systems to machine learning, describe architectural patterns that place an explanation layer between a detection model and the analyst, and discuss how explanations may shorten investigations, support analyst feedback, and strengthen model governance. One study reports that pairing ensemble anomaly detection with XAI reduced average analysis time from 4.2 hours to 35 minutes; we treat this as a single, unreplicated result. The evidence base is small, relies on single studies, and includes working papers and journals of uneven rigor, and it offers no shared benchmarks or analyst-centred evaluations. We close with practical implications for small institutions and open questions for future research.

items.title: Explainable Graph Neural Network Framework for Multi-Objective Discovery of Next-Generation Battery Materials Using Limited Experimental Data
items.abstract: Exploring the vast chemical design space to find better electrode and electrolyte materials is a roadblock to electric mobility and grid scale storage as no laboratory can keep up. While graph neural networks (GNNs) are a promising method for estimating material properties from the atomic structure, limited use of GNNs in battery research is due to three limitations: predictions from GNNs are hard to interpret, they are typically trained for a single target, and they require labelled data which is limited for new chemistries. It can be seen from the criterion-based comparison made that no single of the reviewed studies covers the topic of representation of the graph, Explainability, multi-objective trade-offs, limited-data learning and experimental validation. items.title: Exploring clinician interpretability of AI decision support systems for surgical anatomy recognition
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) decision support systems for surgery hold promise but face barriers to adoption, particularly around the interpretability of their outputs. We conducted an international cross-sectional survey of 47 neurosurgeons to evaluate perspectives on literature-derived explanatory techniques for AI-generated anatomical segmentations, using endoscopic pituitary surgery as a high-risk exemplar. Participants ranked certainty scores, certainty maps, saliency maps, scene similarity scores, and nearest-neighbour illustrations, and rated them using a modified Explanation Satisfaction Scale alongside free-text feedback. Certainty-based techniques were consistently ranked and rated highest - valued for aligning with surgical decision-making by conveying confidence (via scores) and anatomical boundaries (via maps). Saliency- and similarity-based methods were judged less clinically relevant and better suited to educational settings. Therefore, certainty-based techniques appear most acceptable to surgeons for improving the interpretability of AI-assisted anatomical navigation systems, though their impact on trust calibration and performance requires prospective evaluation across surgical domains.

items.title: Exploring Reform in a Progressive, Project-Driven Deep Learning Practical Course: A Case Study of an Intelligent Image Classification System
items.abstract: Addressing issues such as fragmented laboratory sessions, a disconnect between theory and practice, and one-dimensional assessment methods in deep learning practical courses, this paper explores a progressive, project-driven teaching reform centered on the iterative development of an “intelligent image classification system.” The course restructured scattered experiments into four progressive projects focused on modeling from scratch, transfer learning, few-shot fine-tuning, and competition practice. By aligning with the competency requirements of the Lanqiao Cup competition, it promoted the integration of competition and coursework. The implementation incorporated AI programming assistants and large language models, while the evaluation established a five-dimensional formative assessment system covering the project process, use of AI tools, technical competence, final defense, and personal growth portfolios. Pilot results show that all four projects met the predetermined requirements. Students’ engineering practice skills and technical decision-making abilities have significantly improved, and the competition pass rate exceeded historical levels, providing a valuable reference for reforming similar practical courses.

items.title: Exploring the Role of AI in Hybrid Work Within Software Engineering
items.abstract: Abstract This paper reports insights from the 4th International Workshop on Global and Hybrid Work in Software Engineering (GoHyb 2026), in which workshop participants, including Agile researchers and practitioners, explored positive and negative future scenarios of AI-supported hybrid and remote work. Our analysis of the discussion shows that participants viewed AI as especially consequential for hybrid work because it can support task review, synthesis, summarization, and asynchronous coordination across distributed teams. At the same time, they expressed concerns that increased AI mediation may weaken human communication, reduce critical discussion, and undermine psychological safety and social connection. Overall, the findings suggest that the central challenge is not simply adopting AI tools, but shaping human–AI collaboration in ways that strengthen coordination without endangering the human capabilities on which software teams rely. The paper closes with implications for future research on AI-enabled hybrid work in software engineering.

items.title: Exploring the use of artificial intelligence (AI) for corrosion-related tasks: Using large language models (LLMs) to analyse organic coatings images
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have increasingly been applied as a novel and accessible alternative to traditional machine learning (ML). Their main advantage lies in the fact that they do not require model training or data pre-processing; instead, they are guided through natural language instructions. In this study, we evaluate the suitability of LLMs for corrosion-related tasks and introduce an approach that combines LLMs with hard-coded logic to enhance reliability and performance. The methodology was tested on three tasks: classifying images of organic coatings in ‘blister’/‘no blister’ classes, ranking specimens based on corrosion severity, and classifying images into severity classes. The results demonstrate performance comparable to that of trained ML models, with ‘blister’/‘no blister’ classification achieving accuracies up to 0.93. These findings highlight the potential of LLMs, when integrated with expert-driven strategies, as practical and scalable tools for corrosion assessment.

items.title: Faculty and administrative perspectives on artificial intelligence tool integration in higher education using cultural historical activity theory
items.abstract: This study explores faculty and administrative perspectives on the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education at Zayed University–Abu Dhabi, within the College of Technological Innovation. Cultural-Historical Activity Theory (CHAT) is used as an interpretive lens to examine how faculty perceive both the opportunities and challenges associated with AI tool integration, particularly in relation to student engagement and learning. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with faculty members and senior administrative staff to explore perceived benefits, risks, and institutional expectations surrounding AI use. Participants perceived AI as having the potential to support personalized learning and reduce administrative workload, while also raising concerns regarding ethics, assessment integrity, digital dependence, and uncertainty surrounding institutional policy. Several systemic tensions emerged across CHAT components, reflecting misalignments between tools, rules, roles, and expectations in AI-supported teaching. The study highlights the need for clear regulatory frameworks, professional development, and ongoing dialogue to guide ethical and pedagogically grounded AI adoption. These findings contribute to current discussions on how faculty and administrators perceive AI integration in higher education and the conditions required to support responsible and educationally meaningful implementation. This study examines faculty and administrator perceptions and does not directly measure student engagement or learning outcomes. Clinical trial: Not applicable.

items.title: From AI Assistants to AI-Dev-Systems: A Three-Layer Model for Human-AI Collaboration in Agile Software Development
items.abstract: Abstract Context: For decades, integrating new capabilities into agile teams, whether UX practices or emerging technologies, has followed a consistent paradigm: teams remain stable while methods adapt. Applied to AI, this approach produces fragmented tooling, governance uncertainty, and vibe coding : unstructured AI use that prevents cumulative organizational capability. We argue this integration paradigm, successful for disciplines like UX, may be inadequate for AI’s transformative scope. Objective: We reframe AI integration as an organizational design problem: how should teams restructure around AI-Dev-Systems , configured environments of AI agents, workflows, and knowledge bases functioning as shared infrastructure? Method: We propose a three-layer model extending platform engineering: (1) System Teams design AI-Dev-Systems; (2) Platform Teams maintain them; (3) Product Teams develop software within them. Results: Developers shift from producers to stewards monitoring AI outputs. Iteration cycles compress, paradoxically elevating product thinking: when implementation ceases to be the bottleneck, what to build matters more than how . XP practices persist but transform into governance mechanisms for AI-generated work. Conclusion: Teams should restructure around AI-Dev-Systems rather than adopt AI tools, our three-layer model offers a structured provocation to reframe the discourse.

items.title: From Mobile Learning to Artificial Intelligence: Evolving UTAUT Constructs in Educational Technology Adoption
items.abstract: The Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) has played a crucial role in understanding technology adoption in education. This study examines the evolution of UTAUT constructs over three technological periods: the early adoption period (2003 to 2010), the mobile and social media Boom (2011 to 2016), and the artificial intelligence and digital transformation era (2017 to present). Using a one-stage meta-analytic structural equation modelling (OSMASEM) approach, data from 73 studies were analysed to evaluate relationships among key constructs, including performance expectancy (PE), effort expectancy (EE), social influence (SI), facilitating conditions (FC), behavioural intention (BI), and use behaviour (UB). The findings revealed substantial variability across contexts and constructs, with BI consistently emerging as the strongest predictor of UB, underscoring its centrality in technology adoption. The influence of PE on BI increased over time, reflecting technological advancements that improved performance outcomes. The importance of FC in predicting UB also grew, emphasising the role of infrastructure and technical support in adoption. These insights highlight the dynamic nature of UTAUT constructs, providing actionable recommendations for educators, policymakers, and technology developers to align strategies with evolving user needs and expectations in educational contexts. This study reinforces UTAUT’s relevance in addressing contemporary technological challenges.
